overloadPatches.semanticRole: Opens (or re-opens, implicitly closing any existing one) a per-process SQL connection to an external 4D Server, ODBC source, or the internal 4D database, becoming the target of subsequent SQL EXECUTE calls and (if '*' is passed) of code inside Begin SQL/End SQL tags.

jointConstraints.rule: userName and password are grouped as an optional pair in the syntax: pass both together or omit both, not just one.

params.name: dataEntry
params.description: Publication name of 4D database or IP address of remote database or Name of the data source entry in the ODBC Manager or "" to display the selection dialog box

sentinelValues.meaning: Displays the interactive ODBC/SQL connection dialog box so the user can select a data source and enter credentials manually.
Redirects subsequent SQL queries to the internal 4D database (equivalent to closing any external connection).

params.name: userName
params.description: Name of the user registered in the data source

params.name: password
params.description: Password of the user registered in the data source
Applied to Begin SQL/End SQL. If omitted, code inside Begin SQL/End SQL still targets the internal SQL engine regardless of this login; if passed, that code is redirected to the dataEntry source.

constraints: dataEntry also accepts structured prefixed syntaxes documented separately: 'IP:<address>{:<port>}' for a direct 4D Server connection, '4D:<Publication_Name>' for a 4D Server publication name, and 'ODBC:<DSN>' (prefix required in uppercase) for an ODBC data source.
For a direct (4D Server) connection, passing empty strings for userName/password only succeeds if 4D passwords are not activated on the target database; otherwise the connection is refused.
Calling SQL LOGIN again without an explicit SQL LOGOUT automatically closes the previous connection first.
On success the OK system variable is set to 1; on failure it is set to 0, an error is generated, and the internal 4D database automatically becomes the current data source again.
